head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Oilers (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Wednesday. The Oil played last night, and the Rangers are rested. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 16th).
The Oilers’ record (.769) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.622), largely thanks to their finishing. The Rangers’ record (.536) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.23 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Rangers, they get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd), hit a lot (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Rangers’ power play could do real damage when the Oilers are shorthanded. On top of that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Connor McDavid (8 G / 28 A / 36 P in 13 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with 13 points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 13 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL.
Tristan Jarry (3-1-2 / .883 SV% in 6 GS) will likely start for Edmonton, and Dylan Garand (4-5-1 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) for the Rangers.

items.text: The Oilers are newly without Zach Hyman, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.
Sean Durzi has a point in six straight games against Edmonton.
Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
Pavel Dorofeyev has three goals on chances worth about 6.3 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.

NYR.head: Too close to call
NYR.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage, and the Oilers will be without Hyman. The Rangers can tip it if their power play gets going.

EDM.head: Nothing to separate these two
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage, and the Oilers will be without Hyman. The Oilers can tip it if their power play gets going.

calls.head: The schedule did the Oilers no favors
calls.body: The Oilers played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Rangers to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: The Oilers can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Oilers’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Rangers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Oilers tonight.

calls.head: Expect a grind
calls.body: The Oilers play some of the league’s slowest games, and so do the Rangers. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.

calls.head: Keep your head up
calls.body: The Oilers and the Rangers are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
